history.rationale: reproducing test FAILS on buggy and PASSES on fixed; numerical probes are disabled (--no-probes), so the test transition is the whole of the evidence

plans.objective: Build buggy and fixed pandas identically (compiled, same Python, same unpinned era dependencies) so that the four developer-test cases fail on buggy with a real assertion/OutOfBoundsDatetime-expectation failure and pass on fixed. Only the environment is changed; T_dev is untouched.
evidence_used: DIAGNOSIS AND THE ONE CHANGE TO MAKE.diagnosis
assumptions: get_period_ordinal is a Cython (.pyx) extension, so the revision must be built with the compiled recipe; the build command is the editable no-build-isolation pip install from the checkout.

PR date is not stated (null), so no era pin is applied; numpy/cython/dateutil are left to the harness's default resolution. If the build fails on a numpy/Cython API break, a pin step-down is the next iteration.
The Python version is not stated in the context, so python_version is left to the harness default; both revisions use the same interpreter for like-for-like comparison.

The 'Exception ignored in' behavior on the buggy side is expected to surface as a test failure because the developer test expects OutOfBoundsDatetime; if instead the buggy side errors at collection, that is a setup problem to fix in the environment.
